kicker: SubQ Snap, from its technical report

scenes.headline: How a decision model keeps per-token cost flat
scenes.sub: SubQ Snap reads up to 393,216 tokens with sparse attention.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sprig! SubQ Snap is a decision model for very long inputs. Its makers say cost per token stays flat as context grows. Here's what that means.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: A decision model's whole cost is reading the input, so Snap lets each query attend to a fixed budget of positions it selects.
scenes.say: A decision model writes no text, so its whole cost is reading the input. Snap lets each query attend only to a fixed budget of positions it picks.

steps.say: A call sends a state, maybe a whole repository and a few images, plus typed questions.
Everything goes through the layers once. That reading is nearly all the compute.
A decision head turns the final states into a probability for every allowed answer. No output tokens, so output is free.

steps.label: Dense: every past position
steps.say: In dense attention every query reads every position before it. Double the context and each token does twice the work.

steps.label: Fixed budget: a chosen few
steps.say: In a fixed-budget sparse layer, each query picks a few positions from anywhere and reads only those, however long the input.

steps.label: The selector must stay cheap
steps.say: The catch is choosing. If picking means scoring every key, cost grows again. How Snap's selector avoids that is unpublished.
The report's own chart shows parity at sixteen thousand tokens. Below that, there is nothing to skip.
At a million tokens, one layer runs fifty-six times faster than FlashAttention-2.

scenes.title: Dense attention FLOPs over sparse
scenes.note: each is close to length over 16,384
scenes.say: Every reduction in the report's table is close to the context length divided by about sixteen thousand. Each query behaves as if it reads a fixed budget of that size.

scenes.text: Below about 16K tokens the sparse layer saves nothing, so Snap's case rests on its long-context results.
scenes.say: Below about sixteen thousand tokens the sparse layer saves nothing. Short benchmarks test the training. Only the long-context results test the architecture.

recap: Decision models pay only for reading
Each query reads a fixed budget
Long inputs are where it shows
scenes.say: To recap: a decision model pays for reading, Snap caps what each query reads, and long inputs are where that shows.
